Independent | published 2026-09-30T18:10:01Z | via Exa (retrieved 3 Oct 2026) — PA copy
headline: Badenoch: Triple lock is 'current' Tory policy and in 'draft manifesto'

Kemi Badenoch, Conservative leader, to the Press Association:
"We were the ones who brought in the triple lock." (asked if she could guarantee it would remain if Tories returned to power)
"Our current policies are in our draft manifesto. The triple lock is our policy and in our draft manifesto."
"I don't believe this is a policy that even (Andy Burnham) understands. His sums don't add up."
"The reason why everybody is talking about the triple lock is because we don't have growth. If we were growing as an economy, nobody would be talking about the triple lock, and that's why I am focusing on the root cause, which is that we're getting poorer, rather than focusing on a symptom, which is that the triple lock is getting more expensive."
Context: The Independent/PA notes senior Tories incl. former chancellor Jeremy Hunt and shadow foreign secretary Tom Tugendhat have individually suggested the current triple lock is unsustainable.
